pairs.basis: N4659 [expr.call]/9 preserves pointed-to const through ellipsis. N1570 7.16.1.1/2 requires compatible promoted types except listed cases. const void is not unqualified void; literal pointer-to-void/character exception does not cover this actual const void*. Compatibility also fails. This is a standard-text analysis, not a machine-checked formal proof.
pairs.qualification_caveat: Do not import the broader qualified-or-unqualified character/void pointer exception from C 6.5.2.2/6 (calls without prototypes); this call has a prototype and is judged by va_arg 7.16.1.1. Same representation is not compatible type and not permission to remove pointed-to const.

pairs.basis: Identical actual and retrieved type in active profile; ordinary lvalue-to-rvalue conversion only. This classifies just this retrieval, not the surrounding execution.

Pointed-to const is part of the pointer type and remains present after ellipsis conversion. The types are not compatible; neither signed/unsigned nor void/character exception applies. Assignment or ordinary qualification conversion is not va_arg matching; no qualification conversion is introduced by this ellipsis. No dereference or actual const object is needed to trigger the incompatible retrieval rule.

N4659 [conv.prom]/4 permits promotion of fixed-underlying unscoped enumeration to promoted underlying type; uint8_t is unsigned char here and promotes to int. Active AST has IntegralCast to int; GCC static assertions independently confirm int32=int and uint8_t=unsigned char. Profile-specific typedef identities are not a universal int32=int assertion.
